title: Search-o1: Agentic Search-Enhanced Large Reasoning Models

analysis.tldr: Search-o1 inserts on-demand search inside long reasoning traces and separately reasons over retrieved documents before feeding evidence back into the main chain.
analysis.problem: Long reasoning chains can hit knowledge gaps mid-trajectory, while injecting raw retrieved text can introduce noise and disrupt the reasoning process.
analysis.core_idea: Let the reasoning model trigger search when it encounters uncertain knowledge and use a dedicated Reason-in-Documents step to distill retrieved evidence before reintegration.
analysis.agent_loop: Reason → detect knowledge gap → search → reason over documents → inject evidence → continue reasoning
analysis.retrieval_design: Retrieval is demand-driven by the evolving reasoning state rather than executed once before generation; a separate evidence-processing module mediates the retrieved context.
compared_to: iterative retrieval without dedicated document reasoning
analysis.evidence: The abstract reports experiments across complex science, mathematics, coding, and six open-domain QA benchmarks; this bootstrap note does not yet reproduce or verify the full result tables.
analysis.why_it_matters: The important shift is not merely adding search to a reasoning model, but treating external search as an action available inside the reasoning trajectory and explicitly managing the retrieved evidence before resuming that trajectory.
limitations: Search quality and trigger calibration can compound errors across long trajectories.
The bootstrap note has not yet been upgraded to full-paper verification.
